nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (Email, Company, Score). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: sales, support + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Process 'sales' → Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Lead Tracker', matched on leadId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Fast-Track 'support' + Alert
nodes.notes: Posts to a Discord channel via an incoming webhook — no bot token needed, the webhook URL on the credential is the only secret. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Discord webhook URL. Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.

nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Lead Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Sort Leads Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

# Save form submissions: Google Sheets

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers capture-forms work end to end across Google Sheets and Discord.

It moves through 7 working steps, in this order:

1. New Lead Form Submission
2. Route by Work Type
3. Process 'sales' → Google Sheets
4. Fast-Track 'support' + Alert
5. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
6. Merge Routed Work
7. Sort Leads Newest First

## Why it exists

Doing capture-forms work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Lead Form Submission → Route by Work Type → Process 'sales' → Google Sheets → Fast-Track 'support' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Sort Leads Newest First

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Discord aligned by hand for capture forms
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Google Sheets, for capture forms
- Capture forms work where "Route by Work Type" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Capture forms work that only reaches Google Sheets when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Discord in step for capture forms, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Google Sheets or Discord call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 7 nodes in this capture-forms build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a capture-forms run reports once rather than 7 times
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 7 nodes for capture forms before wiring Google Sheets
- 7 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for capture forms

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2 / service account.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your capture forms process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

**Do not log**
capture-forms payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
